explanations.explanation: Home is it. Luke says Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). She opens her front door and lets Him in. Martha, the woman of this house, is the host, and the whole scene happens under her roof.

Close, but no tent here. Luke says a woman named Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). It happens in a village, and the text points to a house. I'd have loved a tent, though, because tent stakes are great for hanging a cookie apron.
Nope, no vineyard in this one. Luke says Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). A vineyard is a field full of grapes. This welcome happens indoors, with Martha holding the door open.

explanations.answer: Sits at His feet listening to Him
explanations.explanation: That's Mary. Luke says she "sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) No tray, no apron, no rushing around. She sits down close and listens to every word.

explanations.answer: Brings Him a bowl of fresh water
explanations.explanation: Good guess, since a guest in a house might get that. But Luke doesn't say Mary brings Him anything. She "sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) Her hands are empty and her ears are open.

explanations.answer: Asks Him to bless the whole house
explanations.explanation: Nice thought, friend, but that's not in the text. Luke says Mary "sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) She isn't asking Him for anything there. She's listening.

explanations.answer: That her sister left her to serve alone
explanations.explanation: Right on. Martha says, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) She's got a lot to do and one set of hands. I think she feels stretched thin, and honestly, who hasn't been there?

explanations.answer: That the house is too small for everyone
explanations.explanation: Not quite. Martha never complains about the size of the house. She asks, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) Her complaint is about being left to serve by herself.

explanations.answer: That His followers came without warning
explanations.explanation: That's a fair guess, but the text doesn't say it. Martha's words are, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) Her question is about Mary, not about surprise guests.
True. Martha says, "Tell her to help me!" (Luke 10:40) She says it straight to Jesus. She doesn't whisper it to Mary across the room. She takes it right to the top.
This one is true, so False misses. Martha says, "Tell her to help me!" (Luke 10:40) She asks Jesus to be the one to tell Mary. She's not sneaking around about it.

True. Jesus says, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things." (Luke 10:41) Hear how He says her name twice. I think that's a gentle way to start. He sees what's on her plate and He says it out loud.

It's true, so False misses. The Lord replies, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and upset about many things." (Luke 10:41) He names what He sees in her. No scolding is written there, just what He says.
One is the number. Jesus says, "But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:42) Martha has many things going on, and Jesus puts one thing next to all of them. That's a short list to remember.
Two sounds neat, but that's not what He says. Jesus says, "But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:42) Martha is worried about many things, and He answers with a single one.
Three is a nice round number, but Jesus doesn't say it. He says, "But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:42) One. If it had been three, I'd have needed three timers and a bigger apron.

explanations.answer: It will not be taken away from her
explanations.explanation: Yes. Jesus says Mary "has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) That's a promise about what she has. Nobody can swipe it, not even a long to-do list.

explanations.answer: She has to set it aside for now
explanations.explanation: That's not what Jesus says. He says Mary "has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) Nothing there tells her to set it down. It stays hers.

explanations.answer: She can have it once the work is done
explanations.explanation: Tempting, since we all say "after the work." But Jesus says Mary "has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) He doesn't tell her to wait. She has it right now.
Not true. Martha asks for that, but Jesus doesn't do it. He says Mary "has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) Mary stays right where she is.

False is right. Martha asks Jesus to tell Mary to help (Luke 10:40), but Jesus doesn't send her anywhere. He says Mary "has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) The text shows no sending at all.
